import React from 'react'
  import { MDXTag } from '@mdx-js/tag'
  import { Playground } from 'docz';
import { Theme as Variant, BootstrapTheme } from './src';
import { DocWrapper } from '../bootstrap/setup/docWrapper';
import { Grid } from './grid';

const layoutProps = {
  
};
export default class MDXContent extends React.Component {
  constructor(props) {
    super(props)
    this.layout = null
  }
  render() {
    const { components, ...props } = this.props

    return <MDXTag
             name="wrapper"
             
             components={components}>
<MDXTag name="h1" components={components} props={{"id":"theme"}}>{`Theme`}</MDXTag>
<MDXTag name="p" components={components}>{`The theme package is responsible for setting up all brand-specific styling. It does this
via a JSON object which is passed into the `}<MDXTag name="inlineCode" components={components} parentName="p">{`<Bootstrap>`}</MDXTag>{` or `}<MDXTag name="inlineCode" components={components} parentName="p">{`<Variant>`}</MDXTag>{` components which
then make the theme available to all child elements.`}</MDXTag>
<MDXTag name="h2" components={components} props={{"id":"variants"}}>{`Variants`}</MDXTag>
<MDXTag name="p" components={components}>{`Since the theme is locally scoped to it's children only, we can override some or all of the theme
from any nested element without affecting adjacent items. This is useful to switch contrasts
from a light background with dark text to a dark background with light text. We do this by
providing a `}<MDXTag name="inlineCode" components={components} parentName="p">{`variants`}</MDXTag>{` key in the theme object with a list of color combinations. The important
thing to note about variants is that they all have the exact same keys. This is so nested
child items don't need to know about its parent container's theme, it just renders
the desired color key.`}</MDXTag>
<MDXTag name="p" components={components}>{`For example the `}<MDXTag name="inlineCode" components={components} parentName="p">{`Paragraph`}</MDXTag>{` paragraph component uses the `}<MDXTag name="inlineCode" components={components} parentName="p">{`text`}</MDXTag>{`
color key, and depending on the theme provided that may be white or a dark gray.`}</MDXTag>
<MDXTag name="h3" components={components} props={{"id":"maintaining-theme-variants"}}>{`Maintaining theme variants`}</MDXTag>
<MDXTag name="p" components={components}>{`Variants are given an intentionally generic key like `}<MDXTag name="inlineCode" components={components} parentName="p">{`a`}</MDXTag>{` or `}<MDXTag name="inlineCode" components={components} parentName="p">{`b`}</MDXTag>{` with the idea that once we
get a full-fledged design system we can then give these names that actually mean something useful.
If we called variant `}<MDXTag name="inlineCode" components={components} parentName="p">{`a`}</MDXTag>{` `}<MDXTag name="inlineCode" components={components} parentName="p">{`light`}</MDXTag>{` instead, things would get confusing when we get to a 'light' variant
with slightly different keys. In the near future, we might come up with a pattern that's similar
to this, something like:`}</MDXTag>
<MDXTag name="pre" components={components}><MDXTag name="code" components={components} parentName="pre" props={{"className":"language-js"}}>{`<Box variant="light.secondary">Hello, World!</Box>
`}</MDXTag></MDXTag>
<MDXTag name="p" components={components}>{`Which would have subtle adjustments based on the second key. Below are all of the variants
for the current theme:`}</MDXTag>
<Grid />
<MDXTag name="h3" components={components} props={{"id":"fallback"}}>{`Fallback`}</MDXTag>
<MDXTag name="p" components={components}>{`When no theme is provided, we use the `}<MDXTag name="inlineCode" components={components} parentName="p">{`defaultTheme`}</MDXTag>{`:`}</MDXTag>
<BootstrapTheme>
  <Grid />
</BootstrapTheme>
           </MDXTag>
  }
}
